1	# Clerk — authentication for Next.js
2	
3	Clerk is a drop-in authentication and user management service. It ships React
4	components for sign-in and sign-up, session handling, and social login.
5	
6	## Install
7	
8	```bash
9	npm install @clerk/nextjs
10	```
11	
12	## 1. Environment variables
13	
14	```
15	NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_placeholder
16	CLERK_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_placeholder
17	```
18	
19	## 2. Wrap the app
20	
21	`src/app/layout.tsx`:
22	
23	```tsx
24	import { ClerkProvider } from "@clerk/nextjs";
25	
26	export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
27	  return (
28	    <ClerkProvider>
29	      <html lang="en"><body>{children}</body></html>
30	    </ClerkProvider>
31	  );
32	}
33	```
34	
35	## 3. Protect routes with middleware
36	
37	`src/middleware.ts`:
38	
39	```ts
40	import { clerkMiddleware, createRouteMatcher } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
41	
42	const isProtected = createRouteMatcher(["/dashboard(.*)"]);
43	
44	export default clerkMiddleware(async (auth, req) => {
45	  if (isProtected(req)) await auth.protect();
46	});
47	
48	export const config = { matcher: ["/((?!_next|.*\\..*).*)", "/(api|trpc)(.*)"] };
49	```
50	
51	## 4. Sign-in and sign-up pages
52	
53	```tsx
54	import { SignIn } from "@clerk/nextjs";
55	export default function Page() { return <SignIn />; }
56	```
57	
58	Email + password and Google sign-in are both enabled from the Clerk dashboard;
59	no extra provider code is needed in the app.
60	
61	## 5. Read the current user on the server
62	
63	```ts
64	import { auth, currentUser } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
65	
66	const { userId } = await auth();
67	const user = await currentUser(); // user.emailAddresses[0].emailAddress
68	```
69	
70	Use `userId` as the stable key when linking Clerk users to your own records.
71	
72	## Why teams pick Clerk
73	
74	- Sign-in, sign-up and account UI are prebuilt components, not code you maintain.
75	- Password hashing, sessions, and social providers are handled by the service.
76	- Free tier covers development and small production apps.

Summary of what was built, on top of the existing NextAuth v5 setup:

**Storage**: replaced the in-memory `users.ts` array with SQLite via Prisma (`prisma/schema.prisma` — User/Account/Session/VerificationToken, standard Auth.js adapter shape + `passwordHash` + `sessionVersion`). Needed regardless of the other features, since magic-link tokens and account state can't live in a process-memory array that resets on restart.

**Magic-link sign-in**: added Auth.js's built-in `Resend` email provider. Sign-in page now has a toggle between password and "email me a link." Verified end-to-end against the real Resend API (fails with a clean "couldn't send" message on the placeholder key, as expected — the wiring itself is confirmed correct).

**Sign out of all devices**: the tricky part. Auth.js's Credentials provider can only issue JWT sessions, not database sessions — so I kept JWT sessions everywhere (for one consistent story across Google/credentials/magic-link) and implemented revocation via a `sessionVersion` counter on `User`. The `jwt` callback checks it against the DB on every request; "sign out everywhere" just increments it, instantly invalidating every outstanding token. Verified live: session dies immediately after the call, current device included.

**`/account` page**: change/set password (asks for current password only if one exists — Google/magic-link users can add one), sign out of all devices, delete account (with confirm step; cascades to linked OAuth accounts). All backed by real API routes, all tested against the running app (signup → sign-in → wrong-password rejection → correct change → re-login with new password → sign-out-all → session confirmed dead → delete → session confirmed dead again).
